Android doesn\'t have a single setting called \"default alarm app\". When you ask Google Assistant to set an alarm, the system either uses an app you\'ve picked before, or shows a chooser the first time. Choosing GT Alarm and tapping \"Always\" makes it the default thereafter.

Pixel ships with the Google Clock app handling alarm voice commands. The first time you say \"Hey Google, set an alarm\", Android may show a chooser if both apps qualify — pick GT Alarm and tap Always. To swap later, open Settings → Apps → Google Clock → Open by default → Clear defaults, then voice-trigger again and pick GT Alarm.

Galaxy phones come pre-installed with Samsung Clock. One UI doesn\'t expose a \"default alarm app\" setting — instead, Google Assistant will show a chooser the first time it fires \"set alarm\" and both apps qualify. Pick GT Alarm + tap Always. Bixby may not honor third-party clocks. Make sure GT Alarm is on the battery-optimization exempt list (the card on the alarm list links to that setting) — One UI deep-sleep can otherwise delay alarms.

MIUI Clock is the system default. Voice-set alarms via Google Assistant will trigger a chooser the first time — pick GT Alarm + Always. Note that third-party alarm apps may not show the alarm-clock icon in the status bar (a HyperOS limitation). Also visit GT Alarm\'s battery card; MIUI\'s autostart and background limits are aggressive and can suppress alarms otherwise.

OxygenOS uses the OnePlus Clock by default. The first \"Hey Google, set an alarm\" should show a chooser — pick GT Alarm + tap Always. Visit the battery optimization card on the alarm list; OxygenOS deep-sleep can delay alarms unless GT Alarm is exempted.

Huawei phones without Google Mobile Services (most models since 2020) don\'t run Google Assistant — voice-set won\'t work via the GT Alarm intent. Native assistants (Celia, Bixby) typically don\'t honor third-party alarm apps. If you have a GMS-installed Huawei (older models), follow the Pixel / stock Android steps.

Most Android phones use the system Clock app by default. When Google Assistant fires \"set an alarm\", the system shows a chooser if multiple apps can handle it — pick GT Alarm and tap Always. The system remembers the choice per-intent.
For alarms to ring reliably while your phone is locked, these permissions must be granted. Tap Fix on any item that\'s not green.
One or more permissions are missing. Alarms may not ring or wake the screen until they\'re granted.
Required to show the ringing notification and to start the alarm in the foreground. Without it, the alarm cannot ring.
Lets the app schedule an alarm at the exact minute you set, even in battery-saver mode. Denied by default on Android 14.

Lets the alarm take over the lock screen and wake the display. Sideloaded apps lose this auto-grant on Android 14 — if your phone screen doesn\'t wake when alarms fire, this is almost certainly the cause.

Optional but recommended. Without it, the phone may delay alarm delivery after several idle days. Alarms set via setAlarmClock() are Doze-exempt either way, so daily users rarely notice — leave at default if you prefer.
Some manufacturers add their own background limits on top of Android. The fixes above cover the standard ones; the steps below are what we can\'t check programmatically.

Stock Android has no extra OEM kill. If alarms still misbehave, double-check Settings → Notifications → Do not disturb → Allowed during DND → Alarms and sounds is ON, and Settings → Apps → GT Alarm → Open by default → make this the default alarm app.

Samsung One UI puts unused apps to sleep aggressively. Open Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → + → add GT Alarm. Verify GT Alarm is NOT under Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps. Then Settings → Battery → ⋮ → Automation → Auto-optimize daily OFF. For the paired Huawei watch, also add Huawei Health to Never sleeping apps. Finally Settings → Notifications → Do not disturb → Allowed during DND → Alarms and sounds ON.

MIUI / HyperOS has the most aggressive background kill. Open Settings → Apps → Manage apps → GT Alarm → Autostart ON, Battery saver → No restrictions, and Other permissions → Display pop-up windows while running in the background ON. Lock the app in the recents drawer (pull down the card → padlock icon) so MIUI doesn\'t kill it.

OxygenOS deep-sleep can defer alarms. Open Settings → Battery → Battery optimization → GT Alarm → Don\'t optimize, and Settings → Apps → GT Alarm → Battery usage → Allow background activity ON. If your model has Advanced Optimization, exclude GT Alarm there too.

Open Phone Manager → Protected apps → enable GT Alarm. Then Settings → Battery → Launch → GT Alarm → switch off Manage automatically and turn ON all three sub-toggles (Auto-launch, Secondary launch, Run in background). On EMUI 9+ this is the main fix.

If your phone is a Chinese brand (vivo, OPPO, Realme, Meizu), look for a Phone Manager or Security app and find a Protected apps / Autostart / Background app list. Add GT Alarm there. On other brands stock-Android settings should be enough.
Separate concern: when you say \"Hey Google, set an alarm\", which app handles it. Tap below for the per-brand steps.
